name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,583

clue.text: Extortion in America? Arab chief audibly unhappy

indicators.note: audibly tells us to take the word as it is heard spoken, not as it is written

blocks.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief, and the title is often pronounced like this
feeling down is feeling unhappy

explanation.surface: A tale of an Arab leader, grumpy and overheard, somehow tangled up in American extortion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the word is American slang; the British pronunciation of sheikh as 'shake' supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a shakedown is a racket of extracting money by threats or blackmail.

clue.text: Special hood is not a nice look

blocks.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: A comment on fashion: wearing a particular hood does not flatter you.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl is an angry frowning expression, which nobody would call a pleasant look.

clue.text: In feral den, teen's cooked but still firm

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the following run of words, waiting to be read out

blocks.note: read straight through the end of feral, all of den and the start of teen's

explanation.surface: A wild teenager in a lair, with something being cooked that stays firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'to the tooth', it describes pasta or vegetables cooked yet still offering some bite.

clue.text: Team's regulars were introduced to six-footer

indicators.note: regulars means letters taken at a regular interval, every other one

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of team
people who were introduced have met

explanation.surface: A sports team meeting someone very tall, a six-foot player.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer sounds like a tall person, but it means an insect, which has six legs. Emmet is an old or dialect word for an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is an ant, and every insect walks on six legs, so it is a six-footer.

clue.text: Volume of unruly mobs in uniform

indicators.note: unruly letters are out of order and have to be marshalled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Crowds of rioters dressed in uniform, as if police or soldiers have run amok.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a single book collecting several works, so it is a volume.

clue.text: Managed rising artist moving into storytelling

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards
moving letters change places, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who managed a rising artist's career, now turning to telling stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving into storytelling' reads like a career change, but moving is the anagram signal working on into alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the act of recounting a story, the telling of events in sequence.

clue.text: Twisted healthy wolf's tail in squabble

indicators.note: twisted here means turned round, so the word runs the other way
a tail is the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: fit means in good health
the final letter of wolf

explanation.surface: Two wolves fighting, one getting its tail twisted in the scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, the same as a petty squabble between friends.

clue.text: Cerebral sort of rascal capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a tinker is British slang for a mischievous child
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A brainy little rogue who wins over people's hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tinker, originally a travelling mender of pots, is also a playful name for a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker is an intellectual person who reasons deeply, a brainy type.

clue.text: Blonde model in US university romance

indicators.note: in places one element inside the next one named

blocks.note: fair hair is blonde
the Ford Model T, so T is a crossword model
Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut

explanation.surface: A blonde model studying at an American Ivy League college and falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is not a fashion model but the Model T car, giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance in its older sense is a tale of fantastic adventure, much like a fairy story.

clue.text: See detective operate chopper

blocks.note: to see someone is to court them
DS is a detective sergeant
to man a machine is to operate it

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a police officer fly a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper suggests a helicopter for the detective to operate, but it means a person who chops trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman works in forests felling timber, so he is someone who chops with an axe.

clue.text: Discover path, then stray from it delivering fruit

indicators.note: to dis-cover is to strip off the covering, so the outside letters go and the inner ones stay

blocks.note: a trail is a path; take away its first and last letters
to sin is to stray from the righteous path

explanation.surface: A walker finds a trail, wanders off it, and ends up bringing back some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Discover here means take the cover off, not find; and the sin is a moral straying from the righteous path.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common kind of fruit used in baking.

clue.text: Body temperature on surface

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the temperature letter follows the other piece

blocks.note: a plane is a flat surface
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Taking a body temperature from the skin, as with a forehead thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call planets, moons and stars heavenly bodies, so a planet is a celestial body.

clue.text: Injury extremely bizarre admits servant

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters are kept
admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of bizarre
a lackey is a footman or servant

explanation.surface: A strange injury that a servant confesses to.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is bruising around the eye after a blow, a visible facial wound.

clue.text: Run! Carnivore's outside in sheep's clothing

indicators.note: outside points to the outer letters only, dropping everything in between

blocks.note: flee means run away
the first and last letters of carnivore

explanation.surface: A warning to escape: the wolf is out there in sheep's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a wolf in sheep's clothing, but the last phrase is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is the woolly coat of a sheep, literally the clothing the animal wears.

clue.text: Very unpleasant Latin curses over setter

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
oaths are swear words
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A setter complaining about being sworn at in Latin, which is very unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means hateful or disgusting, deserving strong dislike.

clue.text: They check papers of old pitmen around area

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the next piece is enclosed by the previous phrase

blocks.note: ex means former
pitmen work down a coal pit
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Inspectors checking the documents of retired coal miners in a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old pitmen' together make ex-miners, and the A sits inside that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners mark exam scripts, so they check the papers that candidates write.

clue.text: Approach adult in bar after mistake

indicators.note: in places one element inside the next one named
after says the bar-and-adult piece comes second, behind the word for an error

blocks.note: a slip is a small error
a rod is a metal bar
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up wanders into a pub after making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a slip road is the short road joining or leaving a motorway, what Americans call a ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is an access road, an approach leading onto a main highway.

clue.text: Cutter spotted with barrels mostly charged

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: saw means spotted
B is an abbreviation used for barrels
laden means loaded, charged with a burden

explanation.surface: Gun barrels spotted being mostly loaded, like a firearm half-ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrels and charged suggest guns, but charged means loaded with cargo and loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw-blade is the toothed metal edge of a saw, the part that does the cutting.

clue.text: Crazy grandma consumed by degrees

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed by, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees
nana is an affectionate word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother eaten up gradually, which sounds mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like 'gradually', but degrees are university qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is informal for going mad, so the word means crazy.

clue.text: Uncertain expressions about animal's howler?

indicators.note: about means around, so the following piece is surrounded

blocks.note: er and um are the sounds people make when unsure
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Hesitant noises made over an animal's howling.
explanation.walkthrough: Howler looks like a howling animal, but it means a glaring blunder; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is a printed error, and a howler is slang for an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Heartily ate without shelter in garden perhaps

blocks.note: without means having no
a garden shed is a typical small shelter

explanation.surface: Someone eating a hearty meal outdoors with no cover in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, so to nosh is to eat with gusto.

clue.text: Red cloak left in fright close to forest

indicators.note: to cloak is to wrap up, so one piece is hidden inside another
in confirms which piece is placed inside the other
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a scare is a fright
L is the abbreviation for left
the final letter of forest

explanation.surface: Little Red Riding Hood's red cloak, left behind in fear near the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Red Riding Hood, but red alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright red colour, so it is a shade of red.

clue.text: More substantial lump in rice melted

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape, so the letters are recast in a new order
in places one element inside the next one named

blocks.note: a hunk is a big lump
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook finding a big clump in a pan of rice that has turned mushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chunkier means thicker or bulkier, having more substance or bulk.

clue.text: Called backward lady 'heartlessly ill-tempered'

indicators.note: backward means the word is written from right to left
heartlessly means with the middle removed, so only the outer letters survive

blocks.note: rang means called on the telephone
the first and last letters of lady

explanation.surface: Someone calls a woman unkindly, dismissing her as heartless and bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly can mean grumpy or cantankerous, like a gnarled, crabbed old person.

clue.text: Menacing sound from grey predator

blocks.note: GR is an abbreviation for grey
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A threatening noise coming from a grey hunting animal, perhaps a wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is a low throaty rumble made by an angry animal as a warning.

clue.text: Short wolfish one maybe found in bed

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: lupine is the adjective meaning like a wolf

explanation.surface: A small wolfish creature discovered tucked up in bed, like the wolf in Red Riding Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not where the wolf hid; maybe flags that this is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a tall spiky garden plant, the sort of flower grown in a border.

clue.text: Spring upon moving edges of cape

indicators.note: moving letters change places, so the word before is rearranged
edges are the outer ends, so only the first and last letters count

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of cape

explanation.surface: Leaping onto the moving edge of a cloak, like a cat at a swirling cape.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to leap suddenly to seize something, which is to spring at it.

clue.text: Hairy Scandinavian works for loose women

blocks.note: a troll is a shaggy creature of Scandinavian folklore
ops is short for opera, Latin for works

explanation.surface: A shaggy Norseman labouring on behalf of promiscuous women.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairy Scandinavian suggests a Viking, but it is the troll of Norse folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop is a dated insulting term for a woman thought sexually promiscuous.

clue.text: Creature's cry near small dwellings ...

blocks.note: a mew is the cry of a cat or gull
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An animal crying out close to some little houses.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mews is a row of houses converted from old stables, often a cobbled lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mews cottages are homes built in former stable yards, so mews are dwellings.

clue.text: ... limps badly approaching school dunce

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are done wrongly and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A dim pupil hobbling towards the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the previous one for the surface only. Eton is England's most famous boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or slow-witted person, much like a dunce at school.
